title: Apple posts stronger-than-expected Q4 revenue in first earnings report for new CEO John Ternus
detail:
Apple posts stronger-than-expected Q4 revenue in first earnings report for new CEO John Ternus
FILE - The Apple logo is illuminated at a store in Munich, Germany, April 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File) · Associated Press · AP Photo/Matthias Schrader
BARBARA ORTUTAY

AAPL
GOOG
AMZN

Trading disclosure

Apple Inc. posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter, giving new CEO John Ternus an upbeat start to his tenure, which began in September. The solid results bucked a downward trend for tech giants this quarter, as companies including Alphabet, Amazon and Intel had disappointing quarterly results.

The Cupertino, California-based company earned $30.71 billion, or $2.10 per share, in the July-September period. That's up 12% from $27.47 billion, or $1.85 per share, in the same period a year earlier. Apple said its earnings included 5 cents per share from tariff refunds.

Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion from $102.5 billion.

Analysts, on average, were expecting earnings of $1.99 per share on revenue of $113.4 billion, according to a poll by FactSet.

Apple recently hiked its prices partly due to a global memory chip shortage brought on by the artificial intelligence boom, which helped drive revenue. Compared with earlier generations, the iPhone 18 costs about $100 more and the price of Macs and iPads also increased in June.

"Apple's strong earnings come in the wake of a recent tech sell-off, as investors question the enormous cost and uncertain returns of the AI boom driven by Apple's Big Tech counterparts," said Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne, adding that record iPhone revenue and strong growth in China demonstrate the resilience of Apple's business.

While its rivals are facing investor uncertainty over massive investments in artificial intelligence, Bourne said Apple's "tepid approach" to AI infrastructure spending helps preserve its cash flow — while partnerships with companies like Alphabet could help Apple to strengthen its AI capabilities without taking on the same financial risks as its peers.

The iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable phone that starts at $1,999, was not yet on sale during the company's fiscal fourth quarter, so it wasn't included in the earnings results. Demand has been strong for the pricey model, even though some users have reported problems that include cracked screens, which Apple is fixing or replacing. Apple is also dealing with supply constraints for the Duo, which went on sale in October, though current earliest shipping dates are for January.

Apple's shares were flat in after-hours trading. The stock had closed down 1.8% at $338.32 in regular trading.

title: Dell Technologies vs. Intel: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Dell Technologies vs. Intel: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:50 PM MST 6 min read
DELL
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors choosing between Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) are weighing two different paths in the hardware market. One is a master of execution, while the other is undergoing a massive transformation.

Dell excels at selling complete IT solutions to businesses, while Intel is undergoing a historic transformation to become a premier semiconductor manufacturer for others. Both companies are central to the digital economy, but they offer vastly different risk and reward profiles for everyday investors looking toward 2027.

The case for Dell Technologies

Dell Technologies designs and sells a wide range of hardware, including personal computers, servers, and data storage solutions. It serves a broad customer base including large global enterprises, public institutions, and individual consumers through a mix of direct sales and channel partners. Approximately 40% of its net revenue is generated through these indirect sales channels, which helps it maintain a global footprint.

In its latest annual report, covering the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $113.5 billion, which was a growth of approximately 18.8% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company reported net income of roughly $5.9 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of close to 5.2%, reflecting the portion of total revenue that the business kept as profit.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is negative 12.8x. This metric compares total debt, including short-term and long-term obligations, to shareholder equity, and this negative value indicates that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 0.9x, while free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, reached about $8.6 billion in total.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures semiconductors that power everything from data centers to personal computers. It is increasingly focused on its foundry strategy, which involves manufacturing chips for other companies among semiconductor stocks. Its primary customers are original equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers who incorporate Intel hardware into their final computing products.

In its latest annual report, covering the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue was around $52.9 billion, representing a slight decrease of approximately 0.5% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company reported a net loss of roughly $267.0 million for the period. This led to a net margin of close to negative 0.5% as the company continues to invest heavily in its manufacturing capabilities.
